title: 3Sum
statement: Return every unique triplet of values from the list that adds up to zero. A triplet must use three different positions, and the same set of values must not be reported twice. Order of triplets and of numbers inside them does not matter.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(16)
    return [[r.randint(-1000, 1000) for _ in range(1500)]]

hints.1_question: If you fix one number, the other two must add up to its negative. Which sorted-array technique finds a pair with a given sum?
hints.2_nudge: Sort the array. For each i, run two pointers l and r over the rest. Skip repeated values so you never emit the same triplet twice.
hints.3_big_hint: Skip i if nums[i] == nums[i-1]. While l < r: if the sum is < 0 move l, if > 0 move r, else record, move l past duplicates, and move r.

known_bugs.name: no duplicate handling
known_bugs.followup: For [0, 0, 0, 0] how many times does your code report [0, 0, 0]?

known_bugs.name: two pointers on an unsorted array
known_bugs.followup: Moving l right only makes the sum bigger if the array is sorted. Is yours?

known_bugs.name: tries every triple (O(n^3))
known_bugs.followup: With 1500 numbers, roughly how many triples is that? Which loop can two pointers replace?

followups: Why do you skip duplicates only for i and after a match, not at every step?
How would you extend this to 4Sum (problem 18)?
